problems.title: Two Sum Problem
problems.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. What is the optimal time complexity using a Hash Map?
options: O(n log n) time, O(1) space
problems.explanation: By storing each number's complement (target - num) in a Hash Map, lookup takes O(1) average time, resulting in O(n) overall time and space.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
problems.description: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum. What principle does Kadane's algorithm rely on at each step?
options: Sorting the array and taking two pointers
Deciding whether to add the current element to the existing subarray or start a new subarray
problems.correct_answer: Deciding whether to add the current element to the existing subarray or start a new subarray
problems.explanation: Kadane's algorithm maintains max_ending_here = max(x, max_ending_here + x), deciding dynamically whether extending or resetting provides a larger sum in O(n) time.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the reversed list. What pointers are strictly required to iteratively reverse in O(1) space?
options: A stack to store all node addresses
Two pointers moving in opposite directions from head and tail
problems.explanation: Iterative reversal requires prev (initially null), current (head), and next (to preserve reference before mutating current.next).

problems.title: Detect Cycle in a Linked List (Floyd's Cycle)
problems.description: Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle. Which algorithm achieves O(n) time and O(1) space?
problems.explanation: Floyd's algorithm uses slow (1 step) and fast (2 steps) pointers. If a cycle exists, they must meet within the cycle loop.

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.description: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree, and return its root. What is the time complexity of inverting a binary tree with N nodes?
options: O(N) because each node is visited once
O(N^2) because each swap takes linear time
problems.correct_answer: O(N) because each node is visited once
problems.explanation: Every node must have its left and right subtrees swapped once, yielding O(N) linear time.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) in BST
problems.description: Given a Binary Search Tree (BST) and two nodes p and q, find their Lowest Common Ancestor. What property allows O(h) navigation without a hash table?
options: Left child is smaller and right child is greater than current root
All leaves reside at the exact same depth
BST is always balanced with AVL rotations
problems.correct_answer: Left child is smaller and right child is greater than current root
problems.explanation: In a BST, if both p and q are less than root, LCA is in left subtree; if both are greater, in right subtree; else root is the split point.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. How does this reduce to a known mathematical relation?
problems.explanation: To reach step n, you can arrive from step (n-1) with a 1-step or step (n-2) with a 2-step: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2).

problems.title: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
problems.description: Given weights and values of n items, put these items in a knapsack of capacity W to get maximum value. Why can't greedy approach solve 0/1 knapsack?
options: Items cannot be broken; taking a high value-to-weight item may leave empty space that wastes capacity
Greedy requires float division which is prohibited in integer arrays
Greedy always produces negative weight cycles
There are no optimal substructures in knapsack
problems.correct_answer: Items cannot be broken; taking a high value-to-weight item may leave empty space that wastes capacity
problems.explanation: Because items cannot be fractionally divided, choosing the greedily highest density item may preclude a better combination of items that completely fill capacity.

problems.title: Breadth-First Search (BFS) Shortest Path
problems.description: In an unweighted graph, which data structure is fundamental to finding the shortest path between two vertices?
problems.explanation: BFS uses a FIFO queue to explore nodes in order of their hop distance from the start vertex, guaranteeing the shortest path in unweighted graphs.

problems.title: Detect Cycle in Directed Graph
problems.description: Which algorithm or color-marking approach is standard for finding cycles in a directed graph using DFS?
options: 3-color DFS (White, Gray, Black) to detect back-edges
problems.correct_answer: 3-color DFS (White, Gray, Black) to detect back-edges
problems.explanation: White = unvisited, Gray = visiting (on current call stack), Black = finished. Re-encountering a Gray node signifies a back-edge, hence a directed cycle.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s. What is the optimal frequency counting space complexity assuming lowercase English letters?
options: O(1) space using a fixed 26-element integer array
problems.correct_answer: O(1) space using a fixed 26-element integer array
problems.explanation: An array of size 26 is fixed and constant space (O(1)) regardless of string length N.

problems.title: Merge Sort Time & Space Complexity
problems.description: What are the worst-case time complexity and standard auxiliary space complexity of Merge Sort on an array of size N?
options: O(N log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space
O(N^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space
O(N) time and O(log N) auxiliary space
O(N log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space
problems.correct_answer: O(N log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space
problems.explanation: Merge sort always divides array into halves (log N levels) and requires O(N) linear merging work per level, needing O(N) buffer memory.
